extracted.intended_audience: Title IX coordinators, school administrators, and institutional legal counsel at elementary/secondary and postsecondary institutions (recipients of Federal financial assistance)
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX grievance procedures for schools
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble and final-regulation guidance on how recipients (ESE and PSE institutions and other recipients of federal funds) must respond to reports of sexual harassment, including required grievance procedures, supportive measures, hearings, accommodations, and interactions with State law and disability obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: State law compliance and preemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients ought, to the maximum extent possible, seek to comply with all State and local laws, consistent with the final regulations. To the extent that a conflict cannot be resolved, the final regulations control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department appreciates comment but declines to add waivers or safe-harbors; see 'Section 106.6(h) Preemptive Effect' for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: grievance procedures apply to Title IX sexual harassment only
rubrics_metrics.description: These final regulations appropriately confine their application only to sex discrimination in the form of sexual harassment, and leave other misconduct under the purview of States and local schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For student or employee misconduct that does not constitute Title IX sexual harassment, the final regulations do not prescribe what kind of disciplinary procedures a recipient must or may use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of formal complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(4) gives recipients discretion to consolidate formal complaints where allegations arise from the same facts and circumstances, so that a single grievance process might involve multiple complainants and/or multiple respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consolidation to address multi‑party situations so one process covers related allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearings and cross-examination for PSE institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where sexual harassment is alleged in the education program or activity of a PSE institution, §106.45(b)(6)(i) requires the recipient to adjudicate the allegations by holding a live hearing, with cross-examination conducted by party advisors (including a recipient‑provided advisor if a party appears without an advisor of choice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision-maker must not rely on statements of a party who chooses not to appear or be cross-examined at the live hearing; the decision‑maker also must not draw any inference about responsibility based on a party's refusal to appear or be cross‑examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of statements from non-appearing parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-makers are instructed not to rely on statements of a party who chooses not to appear or be cross-examined at a live hearing, but also not to draw any inference about responsibility based on refusal to appear or be cross-examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient may proceed to objectively evaluate the remaining evidence (excluding the non-appearing party's statements) and reach a determination regarding responsibility; recipients are not required to 'drop the issue' when a party declines to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer supportive measures irrespective of formal complaint participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures to a complainant regardless of whether the complainant signs a formal complaint initiating a grievance process or refuses to participate in a grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised §106.44(a) requires the Title IX Coordinator to promptly contact the complainant to discuss the availability of supportive measures (§106.30), consider the complainant's wishes, inform of availability with or without filing a formal complaint, and explain the process for filing a formal complaint. The offer of supportive measures is a prompt, non-deliberately indifferent response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative leave for employee respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.44(d), a recipient may place a non-student employee-respondent on administrative leave during the pendency of a grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a discretionary tool to separate employees from contact with students regardless of the outcome of the grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESE institutions: hearings optional and flexible
rubrics_metrics.description: An elementary and secondary school recipient is not required to hold hearings to adjudicate formal complaints; if an ESE recipient chooses to hold a hearing (live or otherwise), these final regulations do not prescribe the procedures that must occur at such a hearing (e.g., cross-examination need not be provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations leave procedural details to ESE recipients when they opt to hold hearings; live hearing-specific requirements apply primarily to PSE recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parental and guardian rights
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.6(g) expressly acknowledges the legal rights of parents or guardians to act on behalf of parties during a Title IX grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A parent or guardian's legal right to act on behalf of a complainant or respondent extends to every aspect of a grievance process, including deciding whether to voluntarily consent to participate in informal resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trauma-informed training allowed within training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may train Title IX personnel in trauma-informed approaches as long as such training also complies with the requirements in §106.45(b)(1)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must still meet the substantive regulatory training requirements; trauma-informed content is permissible but must not conflict with other training mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language assistance and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations expressly acknowledge that recipients may need to adjust a grievance process to provide language assistance for parties; see §106.45(b)(1)(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should ensure parties with limited English proficiency receive appropriate assistance during intake, investigation, and adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution: voluntary, informed, written consent required
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties should only engage in informal resolution when that choice is the result of each party's voluntary, informed, written consent; the Department declines to require parties to attempt informal resolution prior to commencing the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure consent is informed and voluntary before offering or facilitating informal resolution; special care at ESE level (see prohibition below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of informal resolution for employee-student allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised §106.45(b)(9)(iii) prohibits ESE recipients (and all recipients) from providing an informal resolution process to resolve allegations that an employee sexually harassed a student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to grooming and power dynamics, informal resolution cannot be used when an employee is accused of sexually harassing a student.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removals for imminent threats
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(c) authorizes emergency removals of respondents who pose an imminent threat to the physical health or safety of one or more individuals; that provision applies equally to all recipients, including ESE recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may remove a respondent on an emergency basis while preserving Title IX protections and process requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish procedures by type of institution (ESE vs PSE) rather than by age
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department prefers to distinguish between types of institution involved in a sexual harassment allegation (ESE vs PSE) rather than distinguishing by the ages of the parties involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This institutional distinction aims to minimize confusing mixed-procedure situations (e.g., multi-party incidents with differing ages) while allowing recipients flexibility to apply procedures (e.g., ESE may hold live hearings in some circumstances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid retraumatization when implementing PSE procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Even the most rigorous procedures required in PSE institutions (i.e., live hearings with cross-examination) may be applied in a manner that seeks to avoid retraumatizing any complainant, including a complainant who is underage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must implement procedural safeguards sensitively to minimize trauma while complying with hearing and cross-examination requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of existing employees for Title IX roles if no conflict and training provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Any recipient, irrespective of size, may use existing employees to fulfill the role of Title IX Coordinator, investigator, and decision-maker, as long as these employees do not have a conflict of interest or bias and receive the requisite training under §106.45(b)(1)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department does not require recipients to hire third-party investigators or contractors; ensure neutrality and proper training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible evidence inspection delivery methods
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(5)(vi) removes the requirement that evidence subject to the parties' inspection and review be electronically sent using a file sharing platform that restricts downloading and copying, and now permits the evidence to be sent either in electronic format or hard copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may choose appropriate methods to provide access to evidence (electronic or hard copy) consistent with inspection and review requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate grievance processes for sex discrimination versus other discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'prompt and equitable' grievance procedures described in §106.8 must be used to resolve complaints of sex discrimination, while the grievance process in §106.45 must be used to resolve allegations of sexual harassment in formal complaints. Different types of discrimination may require a different process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are not required to address discrimination on the basis of race (e.g., under Title VI) in the same manner as sexual harassment under Title IX; use the appropriate statutory/regulatory process for each discrimination type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to comply with applicable disability laws and coordinate services
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with all applicable disability laws (IDEA, Section 504, ADA) when meeting obligations under these final regulations, including ensuring effective communication, coordination between Title IX and disability services, and accessibility of Title IX information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should coordinate internally (with disability services, housing, academic offices) while respecting privacy; consider obtaining advance permissions to allow disability offices to consult with disciplinary offices; provide information in plain language and ensure websites and communications are accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator responsibility for implementation of supportive measures and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a supportive measure or remedy overlaps with disability accommodations or requires coordination across offices (e.g., changing dorm assignment, re-taking exams), the Title IX Coordinator is responsible for the effective implementation of such supportive measures (§106.30) and remedies (§106.45(b)(7)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This responsibility is intended to ease burden on students needing services and to coordinate actions across institutional units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure effective communication and accommodations for parties with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients should ensure clear communication with students with disabilities (including communication disorders and invisible disabilities), and that students understand their rights under disability law during a Title IX proceeding; accommodations must be provided as required by disability laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical measures include bold-print statements in communications about disability protections, plain-language materials, and making reasonable accommodations so that students with disabilities can participate meaningfully in the process.
